A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Faster and Better 3D Splatting via Group Training. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments with 3DGS and Mip-Splatting, component and sampling ablations, and detailed per-scene results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds comparisons involving Mini-Splatting and LightGaussian, an opacity-controlled rendering experiment, and Gaussian-count trajectories.

M1.justification: Cyclic grouping, caching, resampling, global merging, and opacity-proportional sampling remain unchanged (v1 Equation 4; v2 Equation 10). Changing the recommendation to cache high-opacity Gaussians to low-opacity Gaussians corrects prose to match the existing sampling equation and explanation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate novel-view synthesis on Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, Deep Blending, and NeRF-Synthetic/Blender. The added comparisons reuse these datasets; the opacity sweep changes model attributes rather than introducing another task or data domain.

E2.justification: New Table 8 evaluates Mini-Splatting and LightGaussian, each with and without Group Training, across all four datasets. This substantially broadens comparison beyond 3DGS and Mip-Splatting. Their earlier citations and use as sampling-metric sources did not constitute these full-system comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3.2.2 and Figure 6 add a controlled experiment that varies mean opacity using o_i sampled from N(mu_o, 0.1), holding other parameters fixed. The original training duration, grouping interval, under-training ratio, and merging schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds an isolated opacity-versus-rendering-time analysis, while Figure 8 and Appendix D track active Gaussian counts through opacity resets and merging phases. These focused diagnostics supplement the retained hyperparameter analysis, densification distributions, component ablations, and sampling-strategy comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence levels, or significance tests. Shaded bands already appear in Figure 2; the added shaded curve does not introduce a newly defined uncertainty-estimation or reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–7 and v1 Tables 8–15, renumbered 9–16, retain their values. New Table 8 reports training-time reductions of 13–21% for Mini-Splatting and 24–27% for LightGaussian; Mini-Splatting PSNR decreases on three datasets, including 23.26 to 23.10 on Tanks & Temples. Figure 6 adds rendering times of 2.31 ms at mean opacity 0.35 and 1.38 ms at 0.95; Figure 8 adds Gaussian-count trajectories.

T1.justification: v2 introduces two propositions, explicit independence assumptions, loss-gradient derivations, and transmittance expectation arguments in Section 3.2. New Appendix A supplies the densification proof derivation. These formal additions substantially extend v1's equations and largely intuitive opacity-based reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same Group Training novelty, broad compatibility, improved rendering quality, and up-to-30% training-acceleration claims. The additional evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets caching as preserving geometrically important low-opacity primitives during opacity resets. v2 also corrects the caching recommendation and removes v1's explicit explanation that global optimization without global densification can increase redundancy.

D1.justification: The new opacity experiment specifies its sampling distribution and fixed-parameter control. Conversely, v1's explicit saturation threshold of 0.0001 is replaced by a symbolic threshold. Main hyperparameters, hardware disclosures including the A100 exception, and code-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 34 works remain cited; several bibliography edits only correct metadata. Section 4.3 and Appendix C newly position Group Training as complementary to Mini-Splatting acceleration and LightGaussian compression, extending its stated relationship to those methods.

P1.justification: The methodological narrative is substantially rewritten around proposition, proof, and experimental-validation blocks, with further compression of experimental and discussion paragraphs. An applicability subsection is inserted, and the appendices are reorganized from A–B into A–E. The opening sections and conclusion remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the opacity plot and schematic in Figure 6, the Gaussian-count plot in Figure 8, and comparison Table 8. Existing visual content and table designs are retained, with caption editing, renumbering, and layout reflow; the original visual comparison becomes Figure 7.

improvement.justification: Table 8 strengthens evidence for compatibility with acceleration and compression methods, Figure 6 adds direct evidence about opacity-dependent rendering cost, and the caching correction resolves an internal contradiction. These gains are limited by sparse protocol and uncertainty details for the additions and the proofs' restrictive assumptions. The retained broad quality claims also need qualification given Mini-Splatting's PSNR decreases on three datasets.
